questions.question_text: How many commissioners serve on the West Virginia Real Estate Commission?
questions.explanation: The WVREC is composed of five commissioners appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate. At least three must be licensed brokers with 10+ years of experience.

questions.question_text: A candidate is being considered for appointment to the WVREC. How many of the five commissioners must hold a license under the Real Estate License Act?
questions.correct_answer: Four; the fifth is an unlicensed citizen member
distractors: Three; the other two are unlicensed citizen members
All five must be licensed brokers
Two; the other three are unlicensed citizen members
questions.explanation: W. Va. Code §30-40-6(b)(1) requires four of the five commissioners to be licensed under the article — as a broker, associate broker OR salesperson — and one to be a citizen member who is not licensed. Each licensed commissioner must have been licensed and practiced in West Virginia as their primary vocation for at least 10 years immediately preceding appointment, and every commissioner must have been a state resident for at least six years.

questions.question_text: The Governor appoints a fourth commissioner who belongs to the same political party as three sitting commissioners. Is this appointment valid?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, up to four may share a party
distractors: No, maximum three from one party
No, maximum two from one party
Yes, there is no political party restriction of any kind
questions.explanation: W. Va. Code §30-40-6(b)(2) provides that "no more than four commissioners shall belong to the same political party," so a fourth appointment from the same party is permitted — a fifth would not be. The same subsection requires six years of West Virginia residency before appointment.

questions.question_text: How long is a term for a West Virginia Real Estate Commissioner?
questions.explanation: W. Va. Code §30-40-6(b)(1) provides for "five persons appointed for terms of four years by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate." No member may serve more than two consecutive full terms, and a member continues to serve until a successor is appointed and qualified.

questions.question_text: Who must provide advice and consent for the appointment of WVREC commissioners?
questions.explanation: WVREC commissioners are appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate (§30-40-6(b)(1)). Three of the four licensed seats are direct gubernatorial appointments; the fourth licensed seat must be filled from three nominees selected by the West Virginia Association of Realtors (§30-40-6(b)(3)).

questions.question_text: What type of rulemaking authority does the WVREC possess?
questions.explanation: The WVREC has legislative rulemaking authority to implement the Real Estate License Act, covering licensing requirements, education standards, advertising, trust accounts, and professional conduct.

questions.question_text: Which areas does the WVREC's rulemaking authority cover?
questions.explanation: The WVREC's rulemaking authority is broad, covering licensing requirements, education standards, advertising rules, trust accounts, and professional conduct standards.

questions.question_text: A broker asks whether the WVREC can set its own education standards for pre-licensing courses. What is the correct answer?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, WVREC sets education standards by rule
distractors: No, the legislature sets all standards
Yes, but only for broker courses
questions.explanation: The WVREC has legislative rulemaking authority that includes setting education standards for both pre-licensing and continuing education courses.

questions.question_text: The WVREC adopts a new rule requiring additional trust account documentation. Is this within the commission's authority?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, the WVREC can promulgate rules on trust accounts
distractors: No, only the legislature can make trust account rules
No, trust accounts are regulated by the banking commission
Yes, but only with Governor approval
questions.explanation: The WVREC has rulemaking authority to implement the Real Estate License Act, which includes rules governing trust accounts, advertising, education standards, and professional conduct.

questions.question_text: Can the WVREC investigate a complaint without waiting for a formal hearing?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, the commission investigates before any hearing
distractors: No, a hearing must be scheduled first
Only with the licensee's written consent
Only if the Attorney General authorizes it
questions.explanation: The WVREC may investigate before any hearing. Under §30-40-20 a complaint must be submitted in writing on a form prescribed by the Commission; a copy is served on the licensee, who must answer within 20 days; the Commission may then investigate and must determine whether probable cause exists before it holds a hearing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a power of the WVREC?
questions.correct_answer: Issue, deny, suspend, and revoke licenses
distractors: Set maximum commission rates for brokers
Approve all real estate contracts in the state
questions.explanation: The WVREC issues, renews, denies, suspends, revokes and reinstates licenses (§30-40-7(h)) and may apply to court for an injunction (§30-40-24(a)). It does not prosecute — it brings its information to the county prosecuting attorney, who causes criminal proceedings to be brought (§30-40-24(b)). It has no power to set commission rates.

questions.question_text: How many WVREC commissioners constitute a quorum for the conduct of official business?
questions.explanation: W. Va. Code §30-40-6(g): "Three members shall constitute a quorum for the conduct of official business." Note that West Virginia imposes no congressional-district or other geographic requirement on commissioners — the only locality rule is that each must have been a resident of the state for at least six years before appointment.

questions.question_text: A licensee believes the WVREC overstepped its authority by adopting a new advertising rule. What body granted the WVREC the power to promulgate such rules?
questions.correct_answer: The WV Legislature through the License Act
distractors: The WV Supreme Court of Appeals
questions.explanation: The WVREC's authority to promulgate rules and regulations comes from the WV Legislature through the Real Estate License Act (WV Code 30-40). The commission acts under legislative delegation.

questions.question_text: In addition to licensing, the WVREC performs which regulatory function?
questions.explanation: Beyond licensing, the WVREC performs compliance audits on brokerage offices and education providers (§30-40-7(q)), makes periodic inspections of broker trust fund accounts (§30-40-18(j)), investigates complaints, and holds disciplinary hearings. One limit worth knowing: a general examination of a licensee's books requires a pending complaint and may not extend beyond the specific violation charged (§30-40-7(k)).

questions.question_text: A new salesperson asks who has the authority to revoke a real estate license in West Virginia. What is the correct answer?
questions.explanation: The WVREC has the exclusive authority to issue, renew, deny, suspend, and revoke real estate licenses in West Virginia under the Real Estate License Act.
